# Independent root audit: fixed-cap planar compactness and attainment



The proof uses fixed finitely many positively spanning planar normals and a common cap fraction c<1/2. It does not change their angles or translate the source. Conic Caratheodory expresses any separating inward normal as a nonnegative combination of at most two of the listed normals. Their caps cover a separated K, contradicting the two-cap mass bound. This correctly proves source interior before using triangles through that source.

The uniform directional constant kappa is positive by compactness of the unit circle and positive spanning. If p=R e is a radial extremum and W the transverse width, the two triangles to transverse extrema have disjoint interiors and total area RW/2. Thus W<=2k/R. The two opposite-projection normals selected using kappa cover K outside a strip of width 2TW, where T=max||u_i||/kappa. The uncovered area is at most 2TW². Consequently R²<=8Tk/(1-2c), with the stated constant and no direction-dependent omission.

For area-one bodies this gives a common compact containing ball. Hausdorff subsequential limits retain area one and cap volumes by dominated convergence; lower-dimensional limits are ruled out first by outer-neighborhood area convergence. Closed cap-vector constraints pass to the limit. The first argument then forces the original source to remain interior.

With rho B contained in a full-dimensional limit K, Hausdorff error e gives (1-e/rho)K subset K_l subset (1+e/rho)K by support functions. Because all cutting lines pass through 0, this gives the claimed multiplicative section sandwiches. Section densities are positive and continuous, so the specified normalized inverse-section objectives attain their minima. The centered simplex exhibits nonemptiness of the particular feasible class. At a minimum of min_i lambda_i, an index attaining that value also gives a global minimum of its specified lambda_i, justifying the contact-star structural consequence.

No polygonal or triangle classification is inferred. This is an ordinary planar optimization statement, not a mixed-integer extremizer theorem.

## Additional explicit source-inradius estimate

The same hypotheses also give rho>=epsilon k/(2R), where epsilon=1-2c and rho is the radius of the largest origin-centered ball in K. Choose a unit inward support normal n with K subset {n.x>=-rho}. Express n by at most two listed normals. Points of K missing both associated closed caps satisfy -rho<=n.x<0. Their area is at least epsilon k but at most 2R rho. Therefore

    rho >= epsilon k/(2R),
    rho² >= epsilon³ k/(32T).

The estimate gives a quantitative source-interior bound on the normalized compact class. Its use of closed caps causes no boundary loss: all lines have planar area zero.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
